title: Health-cost burden, credit response, and confidence form linked evidence surfaces but not a same-episode causal chain
source_unit: Non-pooled SHED panel, CFPB credit panel/regulatory record, and Census HTOPS respondent comparison

denominator.unit: recontacted respondents with care foregoing in both years

observations.method: SHED 2024 and 2025 public-use records linked by shedid; 2025 panel_weight; descriptive transition.
observations.uncertainty: This does not identify a dated bill, institutional response, trust judgment, or causal order.
observations.counterinterpretation: Persistence may reflect illness, access, coverage, prices, repeated needs, or reporting; debt and delayed purchase are not one welfare outcome.

observations.period: 2017 to 2025; CFPB medical collections credit-system route

denominator.unit: CFPB Consumer Credit Panel and federal regulatory record

observations.method: CFPB Consumer Credit Panel report plus current Regulation V legal-status record; separate credit and regulatory evidence.
observations.uncertainty: One credit bureau is incomplete; credit timing does not establish medical-care causation; legal status does not establish household remedy.
observations.subgroup: Consumers/tradelines in the CFPB medical-collections analysis and federal rulemaking.
observations.counterinterpretation: Credit removal may improve eligibility while leaving the underlying bill, health, care, or household sacrifice unchanged.

observations.period: July 15 to August 3, 2026; expense difficulty and institutional confidence

denominator.unit: two disjoint HTOPS expense-difficulty groups; outcome-specific valid cases

observations.method: Census HTOPS/HPS PWEIGHT/PWEIGHT0 and 80 successive-difference replicate weights; same-round descriptive contrast.
observations.uncertainty: Expense difficulty is not health-cost-specific or dated to a bill; confidence can reflect prior identity, party, information, or other material conditions; no causal bridge to SHED or CFPB.
observations.subgroup: Respondents reporting at least a little difficulty versus no difficulty paying usual expenses.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower confidence may precede expense difficulty or reflect a common cause; institution-specific confidence is not generalized legitimacy or political action.

related_sources.claim: SHED supplies same-respondent care-foregoing transitions and financial adaptation outcomes.
CFPB supplies credit-system visibility, reporting response, and legal-response context.
HTOPS supplies an institution-specific confidence contrast by contemporaneous expense difficulty.

boundary: This is a non-pooled conversion hypothesis. It does not establish that a health-cost event caused a credit outcome, confidence judgment, trust change, political action, or legitimacy shift.
